## Refusal census (J264, N-58; rule (4))

The registered families are `city.test.ts`'s minted city and the fast-check families of the four identity test files at
the PR size, where any throw fails the property. Before: the pre-round images in the mirror gave `Test Files  4 passed
(4)` and `Tests  48 passed (48)`. After: the mirror gave 48/48, and the tree's NEAR gave 48/48. **0 refused before, 0
after.** The two sources also transpile to the same bytes, so no refusal class could move. CONFIRMED. The round's new
cases are UNLAWFUL input (a handed-on address of another kind). They stay REFUSE, as a typed RangeError: succession
hands an address only to a fresh entity of the same kind, so no user reaches the class through §11.4's doors (PLAUSIBLE,
by reading §6.3 *Carry-over* and `match`). N-2's input, a live set that repeats an id, is UNLAWFUL too, by §6.3's
never-reused rule. `mint` accepts it, and `liveSetOf`, the one builder of a live set, refuses it. That is the owner's
pending question.
